title: benchmarks.py repro run starts every instance's /kb-research sessions at once with one argv and prompt, and appends each area's cost, tokens, turns, time, models and failure
goal: benchmarks.py repro run [--instances N] [--model M] [--effort E] [--max-turns T] [--area-usd A] [--instance-usd C] [--timeout S] [--dir DIR] starts every instance at the same time, each running one headless claude -p session per area in the briefs' order with one argv for all (stream-json output, --permission-mode bypassPermissions, the gitkraken plugin off by --settings, the instance's --mcp-config with --strict-mcp-config, --model, --effort, --max-turns, --max-budget-usd), in the instance's clone with its env, the project's hooks on and the query log off by its config; the prompt, built from the area's brief row, is the same for every instance and tells the session to run /kb-research on the brief, to push with kbgit.py sync --push, to add no lookup_eval.csv, lookup_heldout.csv or doc2query row and to read nothing under kb/_self/backlog/, kb/_self/reports/ or outside its clone; before each area the clone is reset to its bare's main (a rebase aborted, git reset --hard, git clean -fd), and the bare's main sha is recorded before and after the area; an instance starts no further area once its recorded spend reaches --instance-usd, and records each area left as a failure named budget; each area's result is appended at once as one json line under DIR with the cost in USD, the input, output and cache tokens, turns, tool calls, wall time, model usage, the subtype or failure (budget, turns, timeout, error) and the shas, and a run started again skips each area with a result and retries each failed one; repro run --dry-run starts nothing and prints each instance's argv, the per-instance estimate and each refusal a real run would meet, exiting 0 with no briefs file and 1 only for a briefs problem; repro run refuses to start while repro questions fails or the start commit holds repro_bench.csv; no new test id: the test_bench.py bundle gains a body that runs two instances over two areas with a planted claude, a budget stop and a resume.

gates.question: Does a run again over a directory whose run.json holds another argv, timeout or settings go on, or is it refused?

go on and record each line's own limits
gates.recommendation: refuse it: one results file holds one set of limits
gates.answer: refuse it: one results file holds one set of limits

notes: Premise 2026-10-15: no repro command exists (benchmarks.py has list, run, pool and report). agent_bench.execute hard-codes timeout=900 (agent_bench.py:226), too short for one /kb-research area session (the seven Opus research items of 2026-10-14/15 ran 6-12 min, Sonnet research stories up to 21 min). Precedents to copy: bench_install.s_ingest (headless skill session in a throwaway clone with --max-budget-usd), bench_pool.run_pool (ThreadPoolExecutor, --jobs, --max-usd), Bench.bench_rows. Prompt per area: the /kb-research skill with the area's brief row, the same text for every instance, telling it to push with kbgit.py sync --push and to add no rows to lookup_eval.csv, lookup_heldout.csv or doc2query. The test bundle passes before the work: it pins the new bodies once they are added; the checks that fail before the work are the repro subcommands. Operator decision 2026-10-15 (supersedes the plan's 'caveman user plugin stays on' note): every instance's headless command takes exactly --settings '{"enabledPlugins":{"gitkraken@synced":false,"caveman@caveman":false}}' (verified 2026-10-15: a session with it has neither caveman context nor gitkraken tools). Build this exact value into the instance argv and record it with the run's settings (the run's recorded settings name both plugins off). Sprint and worker sessions are unchanged.
